correctness.rationale: With t=h/(2π) the exact fixed-point equation is K_N u∈Z^N, |u_i|≤t and sin z_i=u_i/t. Distinct u have disjoint torus preimages, with a factor of two per strict coordinate and one per saturated coordinate. The boundary values u_0=u_m=0 force all successive differences equal modulo one to k/m; conversely this residue condition suffices. Order d=m/gcd(k,m)>1 supplies each nonzero fraction of denominator d exactly m/d times, so the class's first radius is floor(d/2)/d. The nonzero integral vectors first enter at 1 and cannot minimize. If m has any odd factor, the uniquely minimizing order is the least odd prime p; each of its p−1 classes has one representative and 2m/p saturated coordinates. If m is a power of two, all m−1 nonzero classes minimize at 1/2; a class of order d has m/d half-coordinate ties, and the 2^(m/d) representatives exactly cancel the 2^(m/d) loss of sine multiplicity at threshold. Above threshold all coordinates are strict and no further lattice vectors enter until a positive norm gap, by discreteness for fixed m. This proves both formulas, also at m=2 and in the m=3,4 examples. The frozen exact-rational verifier checks small residue classes, not the infinite claim; it was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This locates the first genuine departure from the critical-point fixed-set picture of a standard path model, not merely a sufficient small-step bound. The least odd factor or power-of-two distinction changes the threshold and the multiplicity jump; knowing the lift order alone does not give the geometric count at a fold of the sine inverse. The count on both sides of the first birth is a meaningful exact benchmark for large-step dynamics, without stability or cycle claims.
